english.html: cent <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>; and so to embrace the gentler, more humane opinion, and that which tends to the deliverance of the accused <sup class="mk" data-key="n">n</sup>.

notes.gloss: Satius enim esse impunitum relinqui facinus nocentis quam innocentem damnari — better that the crime of a guilty man go unpunished than that an innocent man be condemned: the very maxim Coras translates.

notes.citation: An authentica cited by the incipit Itaque, under a Code title printed C. con. de ſuc. (perhaps Communia de successionibus, C. 6.59) — not identified
notes.original: Aud. itaque. C. con. de ſuc.
notes.gloss: The transcription marks this note an orphan; it is the note for the body's third marker, read {c}. The print's Aud. is read as Aut., authentica. Its bearing on the concurrence of favours could not be verified.

english.html: Following which opinion, as the most equitable, it seems that the conjectures and arguments deduced to the contrary are nothing, or very little. For as to the first, on the number of the witnesses, the answer is clear from what is said above: that to the witnesses deposing for the prisoner, although they are not so great in number, nevertheless more faith must be given — both because they depose things more probable.

One must not look so much to the number and multitude of the witnesses as to the verisimilitude of what they depose <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>; so that more faith must be given to those who depose probable things than to the others, even though these be in much greater number <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.19 (De probationibus), c. Licet causam (cf. X 2.19.9, Innocent III; number unverified); X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. In nostra (chapter not identified)
notes.original: c. licet cau ſam. de prob. c⟨alt:c.⟩ & in noſtra de teſtib.
notes.gloss: Witnesses are to be weighed by the probability of their depositions, not counted.

notes.citation: Digest 22.5 (De testibus), l. Ob carmen (D. 22.5.21, Arcadius Charisius), the last paragraph (D. 22.5.21.3)
notes.original: l. ob carnem. P fina. D. de teſtib.
notes.gloss: Non ad multitudinem respici oportet, sed ad sinceram testimoniorum fidem — where witnesses differ, the judge is to regard not their number but the sincere faith of their testimony, and the evidence that most nearly agrees with the truth. The print's carnem is a wrong sort for carmen.

english.html: As also because they affirm and depose in favour of the marriage, of the children, and of the accused.

These three points were of great consideration for the accused: for in the first place, much more faith is given to two witnesses who affirm some fact than to a thousand others <sup class="mk" data-key="a2">a2</sup>. And next, in things which admit of some doubt, the favour either of the marriage, or of the children, or of the accused makes the balance fall (as was said a little before) to that side <sup class="mk" data-key="b2">b2</sup>: with stronger reason,

notes.citation: Accursius (Accurse) on Digest 4.8 (De receptis: qui arbitrium receperint), l. Diem (l. Diem proferre; fragment and paragraph unverified), § Si plures
notes.original: Accurſe en la l. diem. P. ſi plures. D. de recep arb.
notes.gloss: The Gloss there weighs number against affirmation: two who affirm a fact outweigh many who deny it.

notes.citation: Digest 44.7 (De obligationibus et actionibus), l. Arrianus (cf. D. 44.7.47, Paul); Decretals X 2.27 (De sententia et re iudicata), the last chapter (chapter not identified)
notes.original: l. Arrianus. D de actio & oblig. c. fina. de re iud.
notes.gloss: Both cited at Annotation L, notes e and a: in doubt, the balance falls for the defendant and for the marriage.
